Customer payments

Receipts, and what happens when someone cancels

Email customers a receipt
Which payments get a receipt
Every payment, including renewals
The first payment only
Only payments with a value above zero
Email a confirmation when money is refunded
Name shown on card statements
5–22 letters, numbers, spaces, dots or hyphens, with at least one letter. Sent to Stripe on every checkout, one-click upsell and membership. Stripe may put your account's short prefix in front. Leave blank to use the name on your Stripe account.
What the receipt is called
Heads the document a customer prints. Leave blank for "Receipt".
Refund policy printed on receipts
Printed at the foot of every receipt, so the terms travel with the money.
Email a reminder before a free trial ends
Tells the customer when the trial ends and what the first payment will be.
How long before the trial ends
days before
Email a reminder before a membership or instalment payment
Sent once for each upcoming payment, with a link to update the card.
How long before the payment
days before
Stop access as soon as the first recurring payment fails
Only the access that membership pays for is paused. The moment a retry or a new card pays the invoice, the same access comes back on its own.
When someone cancels a subscription
They keep access until the month they've paid for ends
Access stops straight away
Extra days of access after that
A short cushion so nobody is locked out by a card that failed on a Friday.
days
Take access back when you refund someone in full
Reasons a customer can choose when they cancel

Customers pick one of these, in this order, when they cancel from their billing page. Their answers feed the “People who left” and “What people said when they left” reports. Rewording a reason keeps its history in your reports.

When a payment fails

How often a declined membership or instalment payment is tried again, and what happens when the tries run out.

Who tries the card again
If you choose this site, switch off automatic retries in your Stripe account (Settings → Billing → Revenue recovery → Retries) so a card isn't tried twice as often.
Stripe, using the retry settings in your Stripe account
This site, on the schedule below
Wait this many days before each new try
Whole days, separated by commas. "3, 5, 7" tries three more times: 3 days after the first failure, then 5 days later, then 7 days after that. Up to 6 tries, 1–30 days apart.
When the last try fails
Only used when this site is doing the retries. The customer gets the payment-failed email after every try either way.
Cancel the membership, and end the access it pays for
Stop trying, but leave the membership overdue for me to sort out

Abandoned checkout reminders

A global sequence for every offer. Delays run from the last checkout activity. Purchase completion stops every remaining reminder. Sales are attributed to the last reminder link followed before purchase.

Send abandoned checkout reminders
Who receives reminders
Leave empty for all eligible checkout visitors, or enter specific email addresses separated by commas or newlines. Only people who started a checkout receive reminders. Unsubscribes and suppressions always apply.
